Definition: from G1909 and G3306; to stay over, i.e. remain (figuratively, persevere):--abide (in), continue (in), tarry.
BiblicalUsage: Epimeno means to remain, to continue, to abide — to stay over and not leave. Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. Peter tarries certain days with Cornelius; Paul tells the Colossians to continue in the faith grounded and settled; and Timothy is told to continue in the doctrine, for in doing this thou shalt save thyself and them that hear thee.
TheologicalSignificance: Continuing is the whole of the Christian life: not starting well, but staying — grounded, settled, and not moved away from the hope of the gospel. I believe the staying is the proof, and Timothy's charge is mine too: continue in the doctrine, and save both yourself and your hearers.
